title: Quantum Mechanism of Piezomagnetism in Higher-Spin Altermagnets
abstract: We investigate piezomagnetism in higher-spin altermagnets with easy-plane single-ion anisotropy using a flavor-wave approach. We show that quantum fluctuations of higher-spin collective modes provide a microscopic origin of the piezomagnetic response. For integer spins, the relevant branch softens and evolves into a Higgs-like amplitude mode on approaching the large-$D$ transition, endowing the excitation with a sizable dipolar component and producing a pronounced enhancement of piezomagnetism. By contrast, in half-integer systems the higher-spin branches are progressively separated from the low-energy dipolar sector as the anisotropy increases, which suppresses their contribution to the response. This integer-half-integer contrast directly links macroscopic piezomagnetism to the low-energy fate of multipolar excitations. Our results establish piezomagnetism as a probe of higher-spin quantum dynamics and identify higher-spin altermagnets as a promising setting for quantum magnetoelastic responses.
summary: This work theoretically derives the microscopic origin of piezomagnetism in higher-spin altermagnets by analyzing how lattice distortions couple to magnetic excitations. The key finding is a stark contrast between integer and half-integer spins: integer spins exhibit enhanced response due to a specific excitation mode softening into a Higgs-like amplitude mode, while this mechanism fails for half-integer systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the quantum mechanism by which lattice distortions (piezomagnetism) couple to and are mediated by higher-spin collective magnetic excitations in altermagnets.
main_result: Integer spin systems show a pronounced enhancement of piezomagnetism due to a specific multipolar excitation mode softening into a Higgs-like amplitude mode near the large-$D$ transition, contrasting with half-integer spins where this contribution is suppressed.
method: The analysis employs flavor-wave theory and linear response theory applied to an effective Hamiltonian derived from mean-field decoupling of the spin system. This allows calculating susceptibilities based on excitation modes.
model_or_system: The model is a two-sublattice antiferromagnet on a square lattice with higher spin $S$, governed by an exchange, second-neighbor interaction, and easy-plane anisotropy ($D$). The Hamiltonian is perturbed by small uniaxial lattice distortions ($\delta J, \delta K, \delta D$).

important_parameters: Spin quantum number $S$ (integer vs. half-integer), anisotropy strength ($D$), and lattice distortion coupling constants.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field decoupling of the Hamiltonian, followed by bosonization/flavor-wave theory to describe excitations around the ground state.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how susceptibilities ($\chi_K, \chi_D$) vary with anisotropy $D/J$ for different spins, highlighting peaks near the large-$D$ transition for integer spins. Other figures detail the mode dependence of coupling matrix elements.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the theoretical framework by defining the Hamiltonian and using mean-field theory to establish excitation modes. It then applies linear response theory to calculate piezomagnetic susceptibilities, contrasting the behavior between integer and half-integer spin systems based on the fate of specific multipolar excitations.
why_interesting: The explicit link established between macroscopic magnetoelastic coupling (piezomagnetism) and the quantum dynamics/stability of higher-order magnetic excitations ($\mu=4n$ modes) provides a rich theoretical playground for understanding emergent properties in strongly correlated magnets, relevant to AMO systems exhibiting strong spin-orbit coupling.
